correctness.rationale: For each edge vu, the direct edge and its internally disjoint two-edge routes through common neighbors have conductance 1+t/2. The full graph has at least this conductance, yielding the local inequality with the correct half factor. At a simplicial vertex t=d−1 on every incident edge, giving p(v)≥1/(d+1). A one-attachment outside component can be extended at its attachment's constant potential, so adds zero Dirichlet energy for any terminals in the clique. If a component attaches to distinct neighbors a,b, use terminals v and a at 1 and 0. The clique energy has a unique minimum with b at 1/2. Equality of the full and clique minima would force this same clique potential and zero energy on the outside a-to-b path, which is impossible. This proves strictness of at least one incident resistance bound and the stated iff. The clique with a path attached to another clique vertex attains equality for each allowed (n,d), including the path of zero new vertices when n=d+1. For s=diag(L^+), resistance row sums are n s+tr(L^+)1 and p=1/n+(Ls)/2, using LL^+=I−J/n. Connectedness thus gives the stated regularity equivalence and average; a simplicial vertex with d≤n−2 has the positive claimed gap. A simplicial vertex of degree n−1 forces completeness, and every nonempty chordal graph has a simplicial vertex. The complete graph satisfies resistance regularity by symmetry. Inspected source checker and its exact spanning-tree enumeration method without executing it; the classification uses the unrestricted proof, not small graph enumeration.

value.rationale: The simple local lower estimate becomes useful by identifying precisely which external components destroy sharpness, constructing all feasible order/degree pairs at equality, and ruling out noncomplete resistance-regular graphs whenever they have a simplicial vertex.
